consensus_summary: Nineveh is primarily the wicked pagan/Gentile city that repents at Jonah’s preaching, receiving mercy and whose men rise in judgment to condemn the unrepentant (Jonah; Matt 12:41/Luke 11:32); commonly or co-equally it is also the violent arrogant empire under irreversible judgment and destruction (Nahum, Zephaniah).
book_summary: A great city of the sea representing gentile peoples who repent and rise in judgment.
consensus_core_identification: repentant Gentile/pagan city (symbol of repentance, mercy to the nations, and men who rise in judgment)
book_core_identification: gentile peoples who repent and rise in judgment (as a great city of the sea)
boundary_disagreement: Book retains only the Jonah/Matthew repentance-and-rising motif and adds the non-standard ‘city of the sea’ descriptor, while consensus regularly extends the same city to the common/co-primary Nahum–Zephaniah ‘bloody city’ of irreversible imperial judgment.
material_contradiction: None; the book does not deny the destruction symbolism, it simply omits it.
rationale: Minimum cores both center on the repentant Gentiles of Jonah who, per Jesus, rise in judgment; the book therefore preserves the consensus’s primary referent. It nevertheless refines by narrowing extension and precision: it excludes the equally attested judgment-destruction strand and introduces ‘of the sea,’ producing a real boundary disagreement without core replacement.
strongest_objection: The dual (repentance + irreversible judgment) portrait is settled across the consensus; omitting half of it plus the unsupported ‘city of the sea’ label makes the entry incomplete relative to the shared tradition.
